newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.

"The interbank rate slipped slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to easier but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.10/2.05 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.13/2.08 percent but one-year was unchanged from Friday's yield of 1.65/1.60 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 was unchanged from last Friday's close of S$99.27/99.32.
September 2001 ended at S$99.28/99.33 against Friday's S$99.27/99.32 and June 2003 at S$98.85/98.90 versus S$98.80/98.85.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent from last Friday's 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent.
